card.name: Brazilian Zouk
card.tagline: Sensual partner dance evolved from lambada, danced to zouk.
card.profile: Brazilian Zouk is a partner dance that began in Brazil in the early 1990s when lambada dancers, losing access to lambada music, adapted their movements to slower Caribbean zouk music (e.g. Kassav'). Structured for teaching at Jaime Aroxa's Rio school by Renata Pecanha and Adilio Porto, it features undulating upper-body movement, body isolations, tilted turns, dips and whip-like head movements. Main substyles: Traditional/Rio-style, Lambazouk (Porto Seguro), and Neo/Modern zouk (English Wikipedia).
card.insight: The name distinguishes the Brazilian dance from Caribbean zouk music; today 'zouk' in dance contexts usually means Brazilian Zouk, danced worldwide (English Wikipedia).
